{{short description|German chemistry professor}}
'''Brigitte Eisenmann''' (10 April 1942 – 26 April 2011) was a German chemist and a professor at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011">{{Cite journal|date=2011|title=Personalnachrichten|url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/NACHRCHEM.2011.59.7-8.753/html|journal=Nachrichten aus der Chemie|volume=59|issue=7–8|pages=753–759|doi=10.1515/NACHRCHEM.2011.59.7-8.753|issn=1868-0054|doi-broken-date=11 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Geschichte der anorganischen chemie: die Entwicklung einer Wissenschaft in Deutschland von Döbereiner bis heute|last=Werner|first=Helmut|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2016|isbn=978-3-527-69300-9|location=Weinheim, Germany|oclc=964358572}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://grabsteine.genealogy.net/tomb.php?cem=3499&tomb=1295&b=E&lang=fr|title=Pierres tombales: Alter Friedhof -teilweise-, Darmstadt|website=grabsteine.genealogy.net|access-date=16 March 2019}}</ref> She was the first woman professor for Chemistry at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tu-darmstadt.de/media/illustrationen/referat_kommunikation/publikationen_km/hoch3/pdf/hoch3_2008_4.pdf|title=Nie mehr Exotenstatus|date=2008|work=Hoch 3|access-date=16 March 2019|page=7}}</ref> Together with [[Herbert Schäfer (chemist)|Herbert Schäfer]], she extended the definition of [[Zintl phase]]s.<ref name="Schäfer-1973">{{Cite journal|last1=Schäfer|first1=Herbert|last2=Eisenmann|first2=Brigitte|last3=Müller|first3=Wiking|date=1973|title=Zintl Phases: Transitions between Metallic and Ionic Bonding|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|language=en|volume=12|issue=9|pages=694–712|doi=10.1002/anie.197306941|issn=1521-3773}}</ref>

== Life ==
Eisenmann studied chemistry at [[LMU Munich]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> She finished her dissertation "Zur Strukturchemie binärer und ternärer Verbindungen von Erdalkalimetallen mit Elementen der IV. Hauptgruppe" in the group of [[Armin Weiss]] in 1971.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> Shortly after, she started researching in the newly established group of Herbert Schäfer at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> Together with him, she performed research on Zintl phases. At first, Eisenmann worked as a research assistant.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> A year later, she worked as a Dozentin.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> Three years later, she became Akademische Oberrätin.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> In 1986, Herbert Schäfer died and Eisenmann continued their joint work.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> Furthermore, she established her own research profile.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> In 1990, she habilitated with the work "Zintlphasen mit komplexen Anionen".<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> She later became an extraordinary professor.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> She was the first female professor for Chemistry at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]].<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> She also contributed to the [[Landolt–Börnstein]].

== Research ==
She discovered the Si<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> butterfly anion in Ba<sub>3</sub>Si<sub>4</sub> during her work on her dissertation.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Eisenmann|first1=B.|last2=Janzon|first2=K. H.|last3=Schäfer|first3=Herbert|last4=Weiss|first4=Armin|date=1 April 1969|title=Notizen: Zur Kenntnis von Ba<sub>3</sub>Si<sub>4</sub>|journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung B|volume=24|issue=4|pages=457–458|doi=10.1515/znb-1969-0421|s2cid=96020633|issn=1865-7117|doi-access=free}}</ref> Furthermore, she and Herbert Schäfer extended the definition of Zintl phases:<ref name="Schäfer-1973" /> In their definition, Zintl phases are intermetallic compounds with a pronounced heteropolar bonding contribution. Furthermore, their anion partial lattices should obey the (8-N) rule.<ref name="Schäfer-1973" /> The latter was newly introduced to the definition of Zintl phases.<ref name="Nachrichten aus der Chemie-2011" /> Up to today, this work is cited more than 300 times.
